system.name: AgentHarm
system.one_liner: A benchmark of explicitly malicious multi-step agent tasks, each with a benign counterpart, measuring whether LLM agents refuse harmful tool-use requests.

content.variant_note: two mirrored lanes (harmful and benign request) feed identical agent icons that loop through tool calls into one shared panel of tool icons
content.argues: A safe agent should refuse harmful multi-step tool requests yet help with their benign counterparts, using the same pool of tools.
content.subject: A hacker and a benign user send requests to an LLM agent whose replies differ, then the agent loops through tool calls over a shared set of proxy tools.

content.reading_order: Starts at the hacker and thought cloud top left, follows the grey arrow to the agent and its reply bubbles, then the tool-call loop and the yellow tool panel; the benign lane below repeats the path.

layout.arrangement_note: Two mirrored horizontal lanes, harmful request on top and benign request below, each running left to right: user pictogram, grey arrow, robot agent with reply bubble, tool-calling loop. A single tall yellow rounded panel of tool icons closes both lanes at the right. No frames or lane dividers; whitespace separates the lanes.

new_tags.name: thought-cloud-pictograms
new_tags.what: a cloud of small pictograms over a user figure showing what they intend or which categories their requests fall in, without text

lessons.what_to_learn: Tell a safety benchmark's setting with two mirrored lanes that use the same agent icon, so only the request pictogram and the green or pink reply bubble change, and close both lanes with one shared tinted panel of tool icons.
lessons.suits: benchmarks or safety evaluations that pair a harmful and a benign version of the same tool-using agent task, where icons can replace boxes.

evidence: AgentHarm evaluates the performance of LLM agents that have to execute multi-step tool calls to fulfill user requests.
Each behavior has a harmful and benign counterpart.
We focus on the setting where the user makes explicitly harmful requests (direct prompting attacks).

summary: AgentHarm is a benchmark of explicitly malicious multi-step tasks for LLM agents that call tools, each with a benign counterpart. Figure 1 is a pictogram scene in two mirrored lanes: a hooded hacker with a laptop and a thought cloud of harm icons sends a harmful request, a headset user sends a benign one, each to an identical robot-head LLM agent. Reply bubbles carry the verdict: a green 'I'm sorry...' with a halo emoji and a pink 'Sure...' with a devil emoji for the harmful request, a green 'Sure' for the benign one. Each agent then loops through 'Multi-step tool calling' into a shared yellow panel of proxy-tool icons such as map, terminal, email, onion, web, chat and servers. Flat cartoon icons, grey block arrows and almost no text carry the setting.
summary_zh: AgentHarm 是衡量 LLM 智能体有害性的基准。图1用卡通图标画出上下两条对称通道：黑客发出有害请求，戴耳机的用户发出正常请求，同一个机器人智能体用绿色或粉色气泡表示拒绝或顺从，再经多步工具调用循环进入右侧黄色的代理工具面板。
notes: Prior kinds actor-interaction and side-by-side-contrast kept; scope-overview added because the thought cloud and the tool grid hint at the extent of harm categories and tools. The schema has no marker kind for verdict emoji or ellipsis dots, recorded as other. Harm-category and tool icons are unlabelled; their meanings are described by what they depict, not matched to the paper's category list. The emoji are text glyphs; all other icons are bitmaps according to the digest.
